1.Introduction
Prim's Algorithm is a greedy algorithm used to find the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) of a
connected and weighted graph. A Minimum Spanning Tree is a subset of edges that connects all
vertices of the graph with the minimum possible total weight and without forming any cycles.
The algorithm starts from any vertex and repeatedly selects the minimum-weight edge that connects a
visited vertex to an unvisited vertex. This process continues until all vertices are included in the
spanning tree.
Prim's Algorithm is widely used in designing communication networks, transportation networks,
electrical networks, and other optimization problems.

2. Objectives
• To understand the concept of Minimum Spanning Tree.
• To implement Prim's Algorithm using the C programming language.
• To determine the minimum cost required to connect all vertices of a graph.

3. Key Terms
• Graph: A collection of vertices and edges.
• Weighted Graph: A graph in which each edge has a cost or weight.
• Spanning Tree: A tree that connects all vertices of a graph.
• Minimum Spanning Tree (MST): A spanning tree having the minimum total edge weight.

4. Algorithm
Algorithm: Prim's Algorithm
Input: Cost matrix of a connected weighted graph having n vertices.
Output: Minimum Spanning Tree and its minimum cost.

Step 1:
Start the algorithm.
Step 2:
Read the number of vertices n.
Step 3:
Read the cost adjacency matrix of the graph.
Step 4:
Replace all diagonal elements and zero values (indicating no edge) with a large value such as 999.

Step 5:
Initialize all vertices as unvisited.
Step 6:
Select the first vertex as the starting vertex and mark it as visited.
Step 7:
Set the number of edges selected ne = 1.
Step 8:
Repeat the following steps until ne < n:
1. Set min = 999.
2. Traverse all vertices i and j.
3. Find the edge having minimum cost such that:
o The starting vertex is already visited.
o The ending vertex is unvisited.
4. Store the corresponding vertices a and b.
Step 9:
If either vertex of the selected edge is unvisited:
• Add the edge to the Minimum Spanning Tree.
• Display the selected edge and its cost.
• Add the edge cost to the total minimum cost.
• Mark the new vertex as visited.
• Increment the edge count.
Step 10:
Remove the selected edge from further consideration by assigning a large value (999) to it.
Step 11:
Repeat the process until n − 1 edges are selected.
Step 12:
Display the total minimum cost of the Minimum Spanning Tree.
Step 13:
Stop the algorithm.
